passage: While repairing the roof of the village school, workers found a tin box wrapped in oilcloth. The stack of hand-drawn maps inside the box ______ every well and footpath that once surrounded the village.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject of the second sentence is the singular noun “stack,” not “maps” or “box,” which are inside prepositional phrases (“of hand-drawn maps,” “inside the box”). A singular subject takes a singular verb, so “shows” (choice A) is correct.

Choices B, C, and D are plural verbs that would agree with “maps” rather than with the true subject, “stack.”
explanation_uz:
Ikkinchi gapning egasi — birlikdagi “stack,” predlogli birikmalar ichidagi “maps” yoki “box” emas (“of hand-drawn maps,” “inside the box”). Birlikdagi egaga birlikdagi fe’l kerak, shuning uchun “shows” (A) to‘g‘ri.

B, C va D — ko‘plikdagi fe’llar; ular haqiqiy ega “stack” bilan emas, “maps” bilan moslashadi.

passage: The route of the city's half marathon changes slightly from year to year. In 2019, the organizers ______ the course along the river embankment for the first time, and runners praised the cool breeze off the water.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“In 2019” marks a specific, finished time in the past, and the rest of the sentence uses the past tense (“runners praised”). The simple past “moved” (choice B) is correct.

Choice A is present tense and choice C is future tense; neither fits an event in 2019. Choice D, the present perfect “have moved,” is not used with a specific past time such as “in 2019.”
explanation_uz:
“In 2019” o‘tmishdagi aniq va tugagan vaqtni bildiradi, gapning qolgan qismi ham o‘tgan zamonda (“runners praised”). Oddiy o‘tgan zamon “moved” (B) to‘g‘ri.

A — hozirgi zamon, C — kelasi zamon; ikkalasi ham 2019-yildagi voqeaga mos emas. D — “have moved” (present perfect) “in 2019” kabi aniq o‘tgan vaqt bilan ishlatilmaydi.

passage: Most frogs have opaque skin, but glass frogs are an exception. In many glass frog species, the skin on the animal's underside is so transparent that observers can see ______ heart beating and its food being digested.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The pronoun refers to “the animal,” a singular noun, and it must show possession (the heart belongs to the animal). The singular possessive pronoun “its” (choice C) is correct; it also matches “its food” later in the sentence.

Choice A, “their,” is plural. Choice B, “it's,” is a contraction of “it is.” Choice D, “they're,” is a contraction of “they are.”
explanation_uz:
Olmosh birlikdagi “the animal” ga ishora qiladi va egalikni bildirishi kerak (yurak hayvonga tegishli). Birlikdagi egalik olmoshi “its” (C) to‘g‘ri; u gap oxiridagi “its food” bilan ham mos.

A — “their” ko‘plikda. B — “it's” “it is” ning qisqartmasi. D — “they're” “they are” ning qisqartmasi.

passage: Five volunteers took turns watching the lake from a wooden hide at dawn, each keeping a separate notebook. Over two seasons, the ______ notebooks recorded more than four hundred sightings of rare ducks.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The notebooks belong to the five volunteers, so the blank needs a plural possessive. For a regular plural noun ending in -s, the possessive is formed by adding only an apostrophe: “volunteers'” (choice D).

Choice A is singular possessive, which would mean one volunteer. Choice B is plural but not possessive. Choice C adds an extra s that standard English does not use for plural nouns ending in -s.
explanation_uz:
Daftarlar besh ko‘ngillilarga tegishli, demak bo‘sh joyga ko‘plikdagi qaratqich shakl kerak. -s bilan tugaydigan oddiy ko‘plikdagi otga faqat apostrof qo‘shiladi: “volunteers'” (D).

A — birlikdagi qaratqich, bitta ko‘ngilli degan ma’noni beradi. B ko‘plikda, lekin qaratqich emas. C -s bilan tugaydigan ko‘plikdagi otlarga standart ingliz tilida qo‘shilmaydigan ortiqcha s ni qo‘shadi.

passage: Hikers who climb the hill above the village can rest beside the ruins of a small fortress. The fortress, built from mud brick at least three centuries ago, ______ now one of the most photographed sites in the district.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The sentence has a subject, “The fortress,” but the phrase “built from mud brick at least three centuries ago” is only a modifier, so the sentence still needs a main verb. The finite verb “is” (choice A) supplies it.

Choices B, C, and D are nonfinite forms (“being,” “having been,” “to be”). None of them can serve as the main verb of a sentence, so each would leave the sentence a fragment.
explanation_uz:
Gapda ega bor (“The fortress”), lekin “built from mud brick at least three centuries ago” faqat aniqlovchi, shuning uchun gapga hali asosiy kesim kerak. Shaxsli fe’l “is” (A) shu vazifani bajaradi.

B, C va D — shaxssiz shakllar (“being,” “having been,” “to be”). Ularning hech biri gapning asosiy kesimi bo‘la olmaydi, natijada gap to‘liqsiz qoladi.

passage: Mastava is a rice soup made with meat and vegetables, and cooks prepare it in many different ways. In chef Sardor Aliyev's version, chopped dill and a spoonful of sour cream ______ added to each bowl just before serving.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject “chopped dill and a spoonful of sour cream” names two things joined by “and,” so it is plural and needs a plural verb. The recipe is described in the present tense, so “are” (choice B) is correct.

Choices A, C, and D are singular verbs. Choice C is also in the past tense, which does not fit the present-tense description of the recipe.
explanation_uz:
“chopped dill and a spoonful of sour cream” egasi “and” bilan bog‘langan ikki narsani bildiradi, demak u ko‘plikda va ko‘plikdagi fe’l talab qiladi. Retsept hozirgi zamonda tasvirlangan, shuning uchun “are” (B) to‘g‘ri.

A, C va D — birlikdagi fe’llar. C bundan tashqari o‘tgan zamonda, bu retseptning hozirgi zamondagi tasviriga mos emas.

passage: Leafcutter ants do not actually eat the leaves they carry back to their nests. Instead, the ants ______ the leaf pieces into a soft paste, grow a fungus on that paste, and then feed on the fungus.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The text describes what leafcutter ants generally do, using the present tense (“do not … eat,” “carry,” “grow,” “feed”). The present-tense “chew” (choice C) keeps the verbs consistent.

Choice A, “chewed,” and choice B, “had chewed,” shift to the past. Choice D, “will have chewed,” shifts to the future perfect. None fits a description of the ants' usual behavior.
explanation_uz:
Matn barg kesuvchi chumolilar odatda nima qilishini hozirgi zamonda tasvirlaydi (“do not … eat,” “carry,” “grow,” “feed”). Hozirgi zamondagi “chew” (C) fe’llar zamonini bir xil saqlaydi.

A — “chewed” va B — “had chewed” o‘tgan zamonga o‘tib ketadi. D — “will have chewed” kelasi zamonga o‘tadi. Ularning hech biri chumolilarning odatiy xatti-harakati tasviriga mos emas.

passage: When the first electric buses arrived in the city, many drivers worried that the new vehicles would struggle on the steep streets of the northern districts. In fact, ______ climbed those streets more smoothly than the old diesel buses ever had.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The pronoun refers to “the new vehicles” (the electric buses), a plural noun, so a plural pronoun is needed. Choice D, “they,” is correct.

Choice A, “it,” and choice C, “this,” are singular. Choice B, “he or she,” refers to a single person, not to buses.
explanation_uz:
Olmosh ko‘plikdagi “the new vehicles” (elektr avtobuslar) ga ishora qiladi, shuning uchun ko‘plikdagi olmosh kerak. D — “they” to‘g‘ri.

A — “it” va C — “this” birlikda. B — “he or she” avtobusga emas, bitta odamga ishora qiladi.

passage: A sudden spring storm left four hikers stranded on a high mountain pass. By the time the rescue team reached them the next morning, the storm ______ and the sky over the pass was clear.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“By the time the rescue team reached them” sets a past moment, and the storm ended before that moment. An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect, so “had passed” (choice A) is correct.

Choice B (“passes”) and choice D (“is passing”) are present tense, and choice C (“will pass”) is future tense; none fits a story told in the past (“reached,” “was clear”).
explanation_uz:
“By the time the rescue team reached them” o‘tmishdagi bir paytni belgilaydi, bo‘ron esa shu paytdan oldin tugagan. O‘tmishdagi boshqa harakatdan oldin tugagan harakat uchun past perfect ishlatiladi, shuning uchun “had passed” (A) to‘g‘ri.

B (“passes”) va D (“is passing”) hozirgi zamonda, C (“will pass”) kelasi zamonda; ularning hech biri o‘tgan zamonda hikoya qilinayotgan voqeaga (“reached,” “was clear”) mos emas.

passage: The old railway station was restored in time for its centenary celebration. Each of the twelve stained-glass windows in its main hall ______ a different event from the history of the railway line.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject is “Each,” which is always singular; “of the twelve stained-glass windows” is a prepositional phrase that describes it. A singular subject needs a singular verb, so “depicts” (choice B) is correct.

Choices A, C, and D are plural verbs that would agree with “windows” instead of the true subject, “Each.”
explanation_uz:
Ega — har doim birlikda bo‘ladigan “Each”; “of the twelve stained-glass windows” esa uni izohlovchi predlogli birikma. Birlikdagi egaga birlikdagi fe’l kerak, shuning uchun “depicts” (B) to‘g‘ri.

A, C va D — ko‘plikdagi fe’llar; ular haqiqiy ega “Each” bilan emas, “windows” bilan moslashadi.

passage: Beekeeper Aziz Hamroyev paints each of the hives in his apiary a different bright color. He does this ______ his bees find their own hive quickly when they return from the fields.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The sentence already has a main verb (“He does this”); the blank needs a phrase that explains the purpose of painting the hives. The infinitive “to help” (choice C) expresses purpose: he does this to help his bees.

Choices A, B, and D are finite verbs (“helps,” “helped,” “has helped”). Placed after “He does this,” each one would give the clause a second main verb with no conjunction to connect it.
explanation_uz:
Gapda asosiy kesim allaqachon bor (“He does this”); bo‘sh joyga uyalarni bo‘yashdan maqsadni bildiruvchi birikma kerak. “to help” infinitivi (C) maqsadni ifodalaydi: u buni asalarilariga yordam berish uchun qiladi.

A, B va D — shaxsli fe’llar (“helps,” “helped,” “has helped”). “He does this” dan keyin qo‘yilsa, ular gapga hech qanday bog‘lovchisiz ikkinchi asosiy kesimni qo‘shib qo‘yadi.

passage: The town's oldest bridge was built of stone in the 1890s. The bridge is narrow, but ______ still strong enough to carry the delivery trucks that cross it every morning.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The blank must supply both a subject and a verb: “but it is still strong enough ….” The contraction “it's” (choice D) means “it is,” so it is correct.

Choice A, “its,” is a possessive pronoun and provides no verb. Choice B, “its',” is not a word in standard English. Choice C, “it,” supplies a subject but leaves the clause without a verb (“but it still strong enough”).
explanation_uz:
Bo‘sh joy ham egani, ham kesimni berishi kerak: “but it is still strong enough ….” “it's” qisqartmasi (D) “it is” ma’nosini beradi, shuning uchun u to‘g‘ri.

A — “its” egalik olmoshi va fe’l bermaydi. B — “its'” standart ingliz tilida mavjud emas. C — “it” egani beradi, lekin gap kesimsiz qoladi (“but it still strong enough”).

passage: During the construction of a new road outside the city, workers uncovered the remains of a small bathhouse. The mosaics on its floor, which archaeologists cleaned and photographed over several months, ______ fishermen hauling nets full of fish.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject of the main clause is the plural noun “mosaics.” Neither “floor” nor the “which” clause changes the number of the subject, so the plural verb “depict” (choice A) is correct.

Choices B, C, and D are singular verbs that would agree with “floor,” a noun inside the prepositional phrase “on its floor,” rather than with “mosaics.”
explanation_uz:
Bosh gapning egasi — ko‘plikdagi “mosaics.” Na “floor,” na “which” ergash gapi eganing sonini o‘zgartirmaydi, shuning uchun ko‘plikdagi “depict” (A) to‘g‘ri.

B, C va D — birlikdagi fe’llar; ular “mosaics” bilan emas, “on its floor” predlogli birikmasi ichidagi “floor” bilan moslashadi.

passage: Very few plants can survive on the crust of a salt flat. Along its edges, however, where fresh groundwater seeps to the surface, ______ a handful of hardy shrubs that store excess salt in their leaves.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
This sentence is inverted: the verb comes before the subject. The subject is “a handful of hardy shrubs,” which refers to several shrubs and is plural, so the plural verb “grow” (choice B) is correct.

Choices A, C, and D are singular verbs. They might seem to agree with “surface” or “groundwater,” but those nouns come before the verb and are not its subject.
explanation_uz:
Bu gapda tartib teskari: kesim egadan oldin keladi. Ega — bir nechta butani bildiruvchi “a handful of hardy shrubs,” u ko‘plikda, shuning uchun ko‘plikdagi “grow” (B) to‘g‘ri.

A, C va D — birlikdagi fe’llar. Ular “surface” yoki “groundwater” bilan moslashadigandek tuyulishi mumkin, lekin bu otlar fe’ldan oldin kelgan va uning egasi emas.

passage: In 2014, a farmer clearing stones from his field uncovered a small bronze mirror with two leaping deer cast on its back. The mirror is the only object of its kind ever found in the valley, ______ that it may have been brought there by traders from far away.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The main clause, “The mirror is the only object of its kind ever found in the valley,” is already complete. The blank must begin a modifying phrase that explains what this fact implies. The participle “suggesting” (choice C) does this.

Choices A and B create finite clauses after a comma: A has a verb with no clear subject, and B is a comma splice. Choice D, “and suggesting,” wrongly pairs the participle with the finite verb “is,” as if they were parallel verbs.
explanation_uz:
Bosh gap “The mirror is the only object of its kind ever found in the valley” allaqachon to‘liq. Bo‘sh joy shu dalil nimani anglatishini tushuntiruvchi aniqlovchi birikmani boshlashi kerak. “suggesting” sifatdoshi (C) aynan shuni qiladi.

A va B verguldan keyin shaxsli gap hosil qiladi: A da fe’lning aniq egasi yo‘q, B esa comma splice. D — “and suggesting” sifatdoshni shaxsli “is” fe’li bilan teng kesimlardek noto‘g‘ri bog‘laydi.

passage: Woodcarver Qahramon Sodiqov's latest commission now hangs at the entrance to a teahouse in Kokand. Carved from a single block of walnut wood, ______
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
option_a: Sodiqov spent three months shaping the door's patterns.
option_b: it took Sodiqov three months to shape the door's patterns.
option_c: Sodiqov's three months of work produced the door's patterns.
option_d: the door took Sodiqov three months to complete.
explanation_en:
The opening phrase, “Carved from a single block of walnut wood,” must describe the noun that comes right after the comma. The door, not the carver, was carved from walnut, so choice D, which begins with “the door,” is correct.

Choice A makes it seem that Sodiqov himself was carved from wood. Choice B places the vague pronoun “it” after the modifier. Choice C places “Sodiqov's three months of work” there, and work cannot be carved from wood.
explanation_uz:
Kirish birikmasi “Carved from a single block of walnut wood” verguldan keyin darhol keladigan otni tasvirlashi kerak. Yong‘oq yog‘ochidan o‘yib yasalgan narsa — usta emas, eshik, shuning uchun “the door” bilan boshlanuvchi D to‘g‘ri.

A go‘yo Sodiqovning o‘zi yog‘ochdan o‘yilgandek ko‘rsatadi. B aniqlovchidan keyin noaniq “it” olmoshini qo‘yadi. C u yerga “Sodiqov's three months of work” ni qo‘yadi, mehnat esa yog‘ochdan o‘yilishi mumkin emas.

passage: Biologists Nigora Saidova and Erkin Rahimov compared two groups of the same lizard species, one living on a rocky island and one on the nearby mainland. The island population, which faces far fewer predators, has longer legs than the mainland one, and ______ members also tend to stay put when a human approaches.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The pronoun refers to “The island population,” a singular noun, and it shows possession (the members belong to the population). The singular possessive “its” (choice A) is correct.

Choice B, “their,” is plural; the nearby plural nouns (“predators,” “legs”) are not the ones that have members. Choice C, “it's,” means “it is,” and choice D, “they're,” means “they are”; neither is possessive.
explanation_uz:
Olmosh birlikdagi “The island population” ga ishora qiladi va egalikni bildiradi (a’zolar populyatsiyaga tegishli). Birlikdagi egalik olmoshi “its” (A) to‘g‘ri.

B — “their” ko‘plikda; yaqindagi ko‘plikdagi otlar (“predators,” “legs”) a’zolarga ega bo‘lgan narsa emas. C — “it's” “it is” ni, D — “they're” “they are” ni bildiradi; ikkalasi ham egalik shakli emas.

passage: Shoira spends most afternoons in her father's glass workshop, pretending to sweep. Whenever he turns back to the furnace, she ______ a single bead from the scraps of colored glass and slips it onto a string she keeps hidden in her sleeve.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The story is told in the present tense (“spends,” “turns,” “slips,” “keeps”). The verb in the blank describes another action in the same sequence, so it should also be present tense: “shapes” (choice B).

Choice A, “shaped,” and choice C, “had shaped,” shift to the past. Choice D, “would have shaped,” describes something that did not happen, which does not fit the narration of Shoira's routine.
explanation_uz:
Hikoya hozirgi zamonda bayon qilingan (“spends,” “turns,” “slips,” “keeps”). Bo‘sh joydagi fe’l ham shu ketma-ketlikdagi yana bir harakatni bildiradi, demak u ham hozirgi zamonda bo‘lishi kerak: “shapes” (B).

A — “shaped” va C — “had shaped” o‘tgan zamonga o‘tib ketadi. D — “would have shaped” sodir bo‘lmagan harakatni bildiradi, bu Shoiraning odatiy ishlarini bayon qilishga mos emas.

passage: The small clock tower above the entrance to the old library has puzzled local historians for years. Neither the architect's original drawings nor the single photograph taken at the library's opening in 1912 ______ the tower, so most historians believe it was added later.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
In a “neither … nor” subject, the verb agrees with the noun closer to it. Here that noun is “photograph,” which is singular, so the singular verb “shows” (choice C) is correct. The present tense also matches “believe.”

Choices A, B, and D are plural verbs, which would agree with “drawings,” the noun farther from the verb.
explanation_uz:
“neither … nor” bilan bog‘langan egada fe’l o‘ziga yaqinroq turgan ot bilan moslashadi. Bu yerda u birlikdagi “photograph,” shuning uchun birlikdagi “shows” (C) to‘g‘ri. Hozirgi zamon “believe” bilan ham mos.

A, B va D — ko‘plikdagi fe’llar; ular fe’ldan uzoqroqdagi “drawings” bilan moslashadi.

passage: Snow leopards move freely across the high mountain border between Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, so studying them requires cooperation. Biologists Aibek Toktogulov and Farrux Nazarov therefore combined both ______ camera-trap records into a single database.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The records belong to two countries, so the blank needs a plural possessive. The plural of “country” is “countries,” and its possessive is formed by adding an apostrophe after the s: “countries'” (choice D).

Choice A is singular possessive, but “both” refers to two countries. Choice B is plural but not possessive. Choice C misspells the plural, which changes y to ies.
explanation_uz:
Yozuvlar ikki davlatga tegishli, demak bo‘sh joyga ko‘plikdagi qaratqich shakl kerak. “country” ning ko‘pligi “countries,” uning qaratqich shakli esa s dan keyin apostrof qo‘shib yasaladi: “countries'” (D).

A birlikdagi qaratqich, lekin “both” ikki davlatni bildiradi. B ko‘plikda, lekin qaratqich emas. C ko‘plik shaklini noto‘g‘ri yozadi; ko‘plikda y harfi ies ga aylanadi.

passage: When a retired music teacher started the town's youth orchestra in 1996, it had just eight players. The orchestra, which now rehearses in the concert hall of the regional college, ______ more than sixty members today.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“The orchestra” is a collective noun that refers to the group as a single unit, so it takes a singular verb. “Today” calls for the present tense, so “has” (choice A) is correct.

Choice B, “have,” is plural, perhaps chosen because an orchestra has many players. Choice C is plural, and “are having” is not used for possession. Choice D is plural and in the past tense, which conflicts with “today.”
explanation_uz:
“The orchestra” — guruhni bitta butun sifatida bildiradigan jamlovchi ot, shuning uchun birlikdagi fe’l oladi. “Today” hozirgi zamonni talab qiladi, shuning uchun “has” (A) to‘g‘ri.

B — “have” ko‘plikda; orkestrda ko‘p o‘yinchi borligi uchun tanlanishi mumkin. C ko‘plikda, bundan tashqari egalik ma’nosida “are having” ishlatilmaydi. D ko‘plikda va o‘tgan zamonda, bu “today” ga zid.

passage: Farmers on the windy plain have long relied on an inexpensive way to protect their fields. Planting rows of poplar trees along the edges of fields ______ the wind that sweeps across the plain and helps keep the soil from drying out.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject is the gerund phrase “Planting rows of poplar trees along the edges of fields.” A gerund phrase names a single activity and is singular, and the second verb in the sentence, “helps,” is also singular. The singular “slows” (choice B) is correct.

Choices A, C, and D are plural verbs that would agree with “rows,” “trees,” or “fields,” which are not the subject.
explanation_uz:
Ega — “Planting rows of poplar trees along the edges of fields” harakat nomi birikmasi. Harakat nomi birikmasi bitta faoliyatni bildiradi va birlikda hisoblanadi; gapdagi ikkinchi fe’l “helps” ham birlikda. Birlikdagi “slows” (B) to‘g‘ri.

A, C va D — ko‘plikdagi fe’llar; ular ega bo‘lmagan “rows,” “trees” yoki “fields” bilan moslashadi.

passage: Archaeologists studying an ancient hillside town have learned a great deal from its water system. The clay pipes that carried water from a mountain spring to the fountains in the town's main square ______ joined with a mortar made of lime and crushed brick.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The long subject, “The clay pipes that carried water from a mountain spring to the fountains in the town's main square,” needs a main verb. The finite verb “were” (choice C) supplies it, giving “The clay pipes … were joined with a mortar ….”

Choices A and B are nonfinite forms and cannot be a sentence's main verb. Choice D, “which were,” turns the rest of the sentence into another relative clause, so the main clause still has no verb.
explanation_uz:
Uzun ega “The clay pipes that carried water from a mountain spring to the fountains in the town's main square” asosiy kesimga muhtoj. Shaxsli fe’l “were” (C) uni beradi: “The clay pipes … were joined with a mortar ….”

A va B — shaxssiz shakllar, ular gapning asosiy kesimi bo‘la olmaydi. D — “which were” gapning qolgan qismini yana bir nisbiy ergash gapga aylantiradi, natijada bosh gap baribir kesimsiz qoladi.

passage: Many writers keep a notebook nearby for ideas, but few have written a whole novel on the move. ______ the first draft of her novel by hand while riding the overnight train between Tashkent and Termez, author Maftuna Ergasheva later called the rhythm of the rails her “first editor.”
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The sentence's main clause is “author Maftuna Ergasheva later called the rhythm of the rails her ‘first editor.’” The blank must begin an introductory modifying phrase that describes Ergasheva. The perfect participle “Having written” (choice D) does this and shows that the writing came before her later comment.

Choices A and B create an independent clause, so the sentence becomes a comma splice. Choice C, “Writing having been,” is ungrammatical and makes no sense with “the first draft.”
explanation_uz:
Gapning bosh qismi — “author Maftuna Ergasheva later called the rhythm of the rails her ‘first editor.’” Bo‘sh joy Ergashevani tasvirlovchi kirish aniqlovchi birikmani boshlashi kerak. “Having written” (D) sifatdoshi buni bajaradi va yozish uning keyingi gapidan oldin bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi.

A va B mustaqil gap hosil qiladi, natijada butun gap comma splice bo‘lib qoladi. C — “Writing having been” grammatik jihatdan noto‘g‘ri va “the first draft” bilan ma’no bermaydi.

passage: Education researcher Kamron Yo‘ldoshev tracks applications to the engineering faculty at his university. Over the past decade, he reports, the number of students from rural districts who apply to the faculty's programs ______ more than doubled.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject is “the number,” which is singular; “of students from rural districts who apply to the faculty's programs” only describes it. “Over the past decade” calls for the present perfect, so “has” (choice A) is correct: “the number … has more than doubled.”

Choice B, “have,” is plural and would agree with “students” or “programs,” not with “number.” (A phrase starting with “a number of” would take a plural verb, but “the number of” is singular.) Choices C and D are plural forms of “be,” and “are/were more than doubled” does not fit the meaning.
explanation_uz:
Ega — birlikdagi “the number”; “of students from rural districts who apply to the faculty's programs” faqat uni izohlaydi. “Over the past decade” present perfect zamonini talab qiladi, shuning uchun “has” (A) to‘g‘ri: “the number … has more than doubled.”

B — “have” ko‘plikda, u “number” bilan emas, “students” yoki “programs” bilan moslashadi. (“a number of” bilan boshlangan birikma ko‘plikdagi fe’l oladi, “the number of” esa birlikda.) C va D — “be” ning ko‘plikdagi shakllari, “are/were more than doubled” ma’noga mos kelmaydi.

passage: Writer Sharif Komilov is remembered today mainly for his travel essays, though his fiction is beginning to attract new attention. First published in 1913 in a small literary magazine, ______
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
option_a: critics ignored his story “The Well Keeper” for decades until a scholar rediscovered it in an archive.
option_b: his story “The Well Keeper” was ignored by critics for decades until a scholar rediscovered it in an archive.
option_c: a scholar rediscovered his story “The Well Keeper” in an archive after critics had ignored it for decades.
option_d: critics' neglect of his story “The Well Keeper” lasted for decades until a scholar rediscovered it in an archive.
explanation_en:
The modifier “First published in 1913 in a small literary magazine” must be followed immediately by the thing that was published. The story was published, so choice B, which places “his story ‘The Well Keeper’” right after the comma, is correct.

Choice A places “critics” after the modifier, and choice C places “a scholar” there; neither was published in a magazine. Choice D is the subtlest trap: it begins with “critics' neglect of his story,” so the noun being modified is “neglect,” not the story.
explanation_uz:
“First published in 1913 in a small literary magazine” aniqlovchisidan keyin darhol nashr etilgan narsa kelishi kerak. Nashr etilgan narsa — hikoya, shuning uchun verguldan keyin “his story ‘The Well Keeper’” ni qo‘yadigan B to‘g‘ri.

A aniqlovchidan keyin “critics” ni, C esa “a scholar” ni qo‘yadi; ularning hech biri jurnalda nashr etilmagan. D eng nozik tuzoq: u “critics' neglect of his story” bilan boshlanadi, demak aniqlanayotgan ot hikoya emas, “neglect.”

passage: Small glaciers in the mountain range had rarely been studied before. The survey that glaciologist Ravshan Mamatov published last year, which compared aerial photographs taken in 1972 with satellite images from 2022, ______ that the range's smallest glaciers lost ice much faster than its largest ones.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject of the second sentence is “The survey”; the “that” clause and the “which” clause after it are both modifiers. The sentence still needs a main verb, and the finite verb “showed” (choice C) supplies it.

Choices A and B are nonfinite forms (“showing,” “to show”) that cannot serve as the main verb, so the sentence would be a fragment. Choice D adds “and it,” which leaves “The survey” without a verb of its own and makes “it” repeat the subject.
explanation_uz:
Ikkinchi gapning egasi — “The survey”; undan keyingi “that” va “which” ergash gaplari faqat aniqlovchi. Gapga hali asosiy kesim kerak, shaxsli fe’l “showed” (C) uni beradi.

A va B — shaxssiz shakllar (“showing,” “to show”), ular asosiy kesim bo‘la olmaydi, gap to‘liqsiz qoladi. D “and it” ni qo‘shadi, natijada “The survey” o‘z kesimisiz qoladi, “it” esa egani takrorlaydi.

passage: Historians long assumed that the merchant ship Nur sank during a violent storm in 1784. But a newly translated letter from one of its passengers suggests otherwise: if the ship ______ in a storm, the crew's final log entry would not have described calm seas and a cloudless sky.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The sentence imagines a past situation that did not happen (according to the letter, the ship did not sink in a storm). In this kind of conditional, the “if” clause uses the past perfect and the main clause uses “would have” + past participle, as in “would not have described.” “Had sunk” (choice D) is correct.

Choice B is the most tempting error: “would have” belongs in the main clause, not in the “if” clause. Choice A (“sinks”) and choice C (“has sunk”) are present-tense forms that do not fit a hypothetical event in 1784.
explanation_uz:
Gap o‘tmishdagi sodir bo‘lmagan vaziyatni tasavvur qiladi (maktubga ko‘ra, kema bo‘ronda cho‘kmagan). Bunday shart gapda “if” qismida past perfect, bosh gapda esa “would have” + o‘tgan zamon sifatdoshi ishlatiladi, masalan “would not have described.” “Had sunk” (D) to‘g‘ri.

B eng jozibali xato: “would have” “if” qismida emas, bosh gapda keladi. A (“sinks”) va C (“has sunk”) hozirgi zamon shakllari bo‘lib, 1784-yildagi faraziy voqeaga mos emas.

passage: For decades, the songs of Khorezm's village wedding singers were rarely heard outside the region. Singer Kamila Usmonova's 2023 recording of twelve such songs, along with the detailed notes she wrote about each song's origins, ______ drawn thousands of new listeners to the tradition.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject is the singular noun “recording.” A phrase beginning with “along with” adds information but does not make the subject plural, and neither do the plurals inside it (“songs,” “notes,” “origins”). The singular “has” (choice A) is correct: “recording … has drawn.”

Choice B, “have,” treats “along with” as if it were “and.” Choices C and D are plural forms of “be,” and “were/are drawn thousands of new listeners” is also ungrammatical.
explanation_uz:
Ega — birlikdagi “recording.” “along with” bilan boshlangan birikma qo‘shimcha ma’lumot beradi, lekin egani ko‘plikka aylantirmaydi; uning ichidagi ko‘plik otlar (“songs,” “notes,” “origins”) ham aylantirmaydi. Birlikdagi “has” (A) to‘g‘ri: “recording … has drawn.”

B — “have” “along with” ni go‘yo “and” dek hisoblaydi. C va D — “be” ning ko‘plikdagi shakllari, bundan tashqari “were/are drawn thousands of new listeners” grammatik jihatdan noto‘g‘ri.

passage: Engineers have begun planning repairs to an old reservoir in the foothills. They warn that the reservoir, which since its completion in 1984 ______ nearly two meters of silt washed down from the eroding hills, now holds far less water than it was designed to.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Since its completion in 1984” describes an action that began in the past and continues up to the present, and the sentence is set in the present (“warn,” “now holds”). That situation calls for the present perfect, “has collected” (choice B).

Choice A, the simple past, does not connect the action to the present the way “since” requires. Choice C, the past perfect, would need a later past event to come before, but the sentence describes the present. Choice D, the future, contradicts the silt that is already reducing the reservoir's capacity.
explanation_uz:
“Since its completion in 1984” o‘tmishda boshlanib, hozirgacha davom etayotgan harakatni bildiradi, gap esa hozirgi zamonda (“warn,” “now holds”). Bunday holatda present perfect — “has collected” (B) kerak.

A — oddiy o‘tgan zamon “since” talab qilganidek harakatni hozirgi payt bilan bog‘lamaydi. C — past perfect undan keyin sodir bo‘lgan o‘tmishdagi voqeani talab qiladi, gap esa hozirgi holatni tasvirlaydi. D — kelasi zamon suv omborining hajmini allaqachon kamaytirayotgan loyqaga zid.

passage: Agronomist Gulshan Nematova spent eight years developing new varieties of cotton for the dry lands south of the Aral Sea. According to her field trials, the new varieties need far less water than older ones; ______ about the same yield with roughly two-thirds as much irrigation.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
A semicolon must join two independent clauses, so the words after it need both a subject and a finite verb. “They produce” (choice C) supplies both, giving the independent clause “they produce about the same yield ….”

Choices A, B, and D are nonfinite forms (“producing,” “having produced,” “to produce”) with no subject. Each would leave a phrase, not an independent clause, after the semicolon. These choices would work after a comma, which makes them tempting.
explanation_uz:
Nuqtali vergul ikki mustaqil gapni bog‘lashi kerak, demak undan keyingi qismda ham ega, ham shaxsli fe’l bo‘lishi kerak. “They produce” (C) ikkalasini ham beradi: “they produce about the same yield ….”

A, B va D — egasiz shaxssiz shakllar (“producing,” “having produced,” “to produce”). Ularning har biri nuqtali verguldan keyin mustaqil gap emas, faqat birikma qoldiradi. Bu variantlar verguldan keyin to‘g‘ri bo‘lardi, shuning uchun jozibali ko‘rinadi.

passage: Decades of neglect had left the old textile market's carved wooden columns cracked and its painted stalls faded. Rather than replace the market with a modern shopping center, the city council voted to restore ______ as a working bazaar for local craftspeople.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The council voted to restore the thing it chose not to replace: “the market,” a singular noun. The singular object pronoun “it” (choice D) is correct.

Choice A, “them,” and choice C, “those,” are plural; they are tempting because “columns” and “stalls” appear earlier, but the council restored the market as a bazaar, not the columns as a bazaar. Choice B, “they,” is plural and is also a subject pronoun, not an object pronoun.
explanation_uz:
Kengash almashtirmaslikka qaror qilgan narsani — birlikdagi “the market” ni — tiklashga ovoz berdi. Birlikdagi to‘ldiruvchi olmosh “it” (D) to‘g‘ri.

A — “them” va C — “those” ko‘plikda; ular jozibali, chunki oldinroq “columns” va “stalls” keladi, lekin bozor sifatida ustunlar emas, bozorning o‘zi tiklandi. B — “they” ko‘plikda va bundan tashqari to‘ldiruvchi emas, ega olmoshi.
